title: Underived vertical pasting for open base change
statement: Let $U'\xrightarrow{g_U}U$ and $X'\xrightarrow{g}X$ form an open-immersion square with open immersions $j:U\to X$ and $j':U'\to X'$. Let $U''\xrightarrow{h_U}U'$ and $X''\xrightarrow{h}X'$ form a second cartesian base-change square, with induced open immersion $j'':U''\to X''$. For every finite commutative coefficient ring $\Lambda$ and $\Lambda$-module sheaf $F$ on $U_{\mathrm{Et}}$, write $b$ for the canonical isomorphism of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change]. After the canonical module-linear inverse-image composition identifications, the composite $$h^{-1}g^{-1}j_!F\xrightarrow{h^{-1}(b_{g,F})}h^{-1}j'_!g_U^{-1}F\xrightarrow{b_{h,g_U^{-1}F}}j''_!h_U^{-1}g_U^{-1}F$$ equals the canonical map $b_{g\circ h,F}:(g\circ h)^{-1}j_!F\to j''_!(g_U\circ h_U)^{-1}F$.

source.place: Tag 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change), composed adjunctions; categories Tags 0B65 and 0DV0

proof.text:
All functors in this proof act on sheaves of modules over the fixed constant ring $\Lambda$. Put $G=g^{-1}$, $H=h^{-1}$, $A=g_U^{-1}$, $B=h_U^{-1}$, $J=j^{-1}$, $J'=j'^{-1}$ and $J''=j''^{-1}$. The square for $g\circ h$ is cartesian: maps to $U$ and $X''$ agreeing over $X$ first give a unique map to $U'$ by the first square and then a unique map to $U''$ by the second. Write $c_{u,v}:v^{-1}u^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(u\circ v)^{-1}$ for the module-linear composition comparison. For the first square its restriction comparison is
$$s_g=c_{g,j'}^{-1}\circ c_{j,g_U}:AJ\longrightarrow J'G,$$
using $j\circ g_U=g\circ j'$. Likewise $s_h=c_{h,j''}^{-1}\circ c_{j',h_U}:BJ'\to J''H$. Let $s_{gh}:(g_U\circ h_U)^{-1}J\to J''(g\circ h)^{-1}$ be the identical construction for the composite square. These are the canonical comparisons appearing in the adjunction characterization of $b$, by [lem-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change-underived-compatibility].

source.place: Tag 03D8 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules); etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change), canonical square comparison

proof.text:
The square comparisons obey
$$s_hG\circ B(s_g)=(J''c_{g,h})^{-1}\circ s_{gh}\circ(c_{g_U,h_U}J):BAJ\longrightarrow J''HG.\tag{*}$$
To verify all the identifications, put $a=g_U$, $b=h_U$ and expand the left side as
$$c_{h,j''}^{-1}G\circ c_{j',b}G\circ B(c_{g,j'}^{-1})\circ B(c_{j,a}).$$
Associativity of $c$ for $(g,j',b)$ gives
$$c_{j',b}G\circ B(c_{g,j'}^{-1})=c_{g,j'\circ b}^{-1}\circ c_{g\circ j',b}.$$
For $(j,a,b)$ it gives
$$c_{j\circ a,b}\circ B(c_{j,a})=c_{j,a\circ b}\circ(c_{a,b}J).$$
Use $g\circ j'=j\circ a$ to substitute the second equality into the expanded product after the first substitution. It becomes
$$c_{h,j''}^{-1}G\circ c_{g,j'\circ b}^{-1}\circ c_{j,a\circ b}\circ(c_{a,b}J).$$
Finally $j'\circ b=h\circ j''$ and associativity for $(g,h,j'')$ give
$$c_{h,j''}^{-1}G\circ c_{g,h\circ j''}^{-1}=(J''c_{g,h})^{-1}\circ c_{g\circ h,j''}^{-1}.$$
The resulting expression is the right side of (*). The associativity law used here is clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition]. By [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear] each module comparison has precisely that abelian comparison as its underlying map. Thus these equations also hold for module sheaves (the forgetful functor is faithful).

source.place: Tag 03D8 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules); explicit associativity calculation for the three triples (g,j',h_U), (j,g_U,h_U), (g,h,j'')

proof.text:
Set $\alpha_{g,F}=b_{g,F}^{-1}:j'_!AF\to Gj_!F$ and $\alpha_{h,AF}=b_{h,AF}^{-1}:j''_!BAF\to Hj'_!AF$. Write $\eta_j,\eta_{j'},\eta_{j''}$ for the units of the extension-by-zero adjunctions. By [lem-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change-underived-compatibility] and [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction],
$$J'(\alpha_{g,F})\circ\eta_{j',AF}=s_{g,j_!F}\circ A(\eta_{j,F}),$$
$$J''(\alpha_{h,AF})\circ\eta_{j'',BAF}=s_{h,j'_!AF}\circ B(\eta_{j',AF}).$$
The same characterization applies to $\alpha_{gh,F}$ because the composite square is cartesian by step 1. Each $\alpha$ is invertible by [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change]. No derived category or resolution is involved.

source.place: Tag 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change), adjunction description of the inverse canonical map

proof.text:
Consider $P=H(\alpha_{g,F})\circ\alpha_{h,AF}:j''_!BAF\to HGj_!F$. Its transpose under $j''_!\dashv J''$ is
$$\begin{aligned}
J''(P)\circ\eta_{j'',BAF}
&=J''H(\alpha_{g,F})\circ s_{h,j'_!AF}\circ B(\eta_{j',AF})\\
&=s_{h,Gj_!F}\circ BJ'(\alpha_{g,F})\circ B(\eta_{j',AF})\\
&=s_{h,Gj_!F}\circ B(s_{g,j_!F})\circ BA(\eta_{j,F}).
\end{aligned}$$
The first equality substitutes step 3 for $\alpha_h$. The second is naturality of $s_h$ at $\alpha_{g,F}$, and the third substitutes step 3 for $\alpha_g$. Substitute (*) and use naturality of $c_{g_U,h_U}$ at $\eta_{j,F}$. This gives
$$(J''c_{g,h,j_!F})^{-1}\circ s_{gh,j_!F}\circ(g_U\circ h_U)^{-1}(\eta_{j,F})\circ c_{g_U,h_U,F}.$$
By step 3 this is precisely the transpose of the composite-map inverse $\alpha_{gh,F}$, transported to source $j''_!BAF$ and target $HGj_!F$. Naturality of the adjunction bijection with respect to these source and target identifications proves that assertion; the displayed formula includes both of them. Injectivity of that bijection therefore identifies $P$ with the transported $\alpha_{gh,F}$.

source.place: Tag 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change); categories.tex Tag 0DV0 (lemma-compose-counits), written-out transpose computation

proof.text: Invert the equality in step 4. Since a functor preserves an inverse, $P^{-1}=b_{h,AF}\circ H(b_{g,F})$. The inverse of the transported $\alpha_{gh,F}$ is the transported $b_{g\circ h,F}$. These are exactly the two maps in the statement, with $A=g_U^{-1}$ and $H=h^{-1}$ and with the source and target comparisons $c_{g,h}$ and $c_{g_U,h_U}$ already specified in (*). This proves the required equality for every $F$ and the given finite commutative ring $\Lambda$.

Step 3: the transpose equations follow from underived-compatibility plus the adjunction; I checked the hypotheses (open-immersion squares, finite Lambda, module sheaves F and AF) and the composite square's cartesian datum from step 1. Step 4: I recomputed J''(P)eta, and independently the transpose of the transported alpha_gh using naturality of eta_j''. They agree, so P equals the transported alpha_gh by injectivity.
